text: The GitLab Terraform CI job was dropped deliberately when CI moved to GitHub Actions, and was not replaced. It used GitLab's managed Terraform state (an http backend plus TF_ADDRESS pointing at the GitLab API), and GitHub has no equivalent. misc/terraform/ is kept, but Terraform is now run by hand. Reinstating it in CI needs a state backend decision first (S3, Terraform Cloud, or similar) plus a Cloudflare token secret. The dead-mans-switch repo, which this CI setup was modelled on, made the same choice.

Stavros wants to modernise the Python and Django stack, but deferred it out of the GitHub CI port (Aug 2026), to be done later as its own piece of work. He asked for Python 3.13 in CI; that is not reachable without the upgrade, because Django 2.0 cannot be imported on 3.12+ (distutils was removed). The blocker is not just Django 2.0 to 5.x. Several dependencies are dead or renamed and need replacing: django-nose (dead, and it is the configured TEST_RUNNER), fake-factory (renamed to Faker in 2016), raven (superseded by sentry-sdk), and brotlipy (abandoned, no modern wheels). The 41 existing tests all pass, so they are a usable safety net for a staged upgrade.

poetry install was silently broken before the GitHub CI port: cbor2 5.1.2 (pulled in transitively by django-webauthin) is published as an sdist only, with no wheels for any Python, and its build fails against modern setuptools with 'No module named pkg_resources'. Fixed by updating just cbor2 to 5.6.5 in poetry.lock. Two operational notes for anyone touching the lock: run poetry update with Poetry 1.4.0, not 2.x, because 2.x rewrites the entire lock into the new format; and any other sdist-only pin in this old dependency set can fail the same way as setuptools moves on.

The tests job's 'poetry install --no-root' step is intermittently flaky, and a rerun usually fixes it. Observed Aug 2026: it failed with a ChefBuildError on curtsies 0.4.1, 'Backend setuptools.build_meta:__legacy__ is not available'. The cause is that CI sets virtualenvs.create false, so Poetry installs into the runner's system Python and downgrades its setuptools to the locked 67.6.0 partway through the install; a later sdist build then runs against the half-swapped setuptools. Which packages are affected depends on install ordering and on whatever setuptools version the GitHub runner image ships that week, so the same commit can pass and then fail with no change to the repo. Rerunning the job is the workaround. Dropping virtualenvs.create false, or pinning setuptools before the install, would fix it properly, but that is really a symptom of the pinned 2020-era dependency set and should be handled by the stack modernisation.

Stavros settled the modernisation targets in Aug 2026: Django 5.2 LTS, Python 3.13, and uv instead of Poetry. Django 4.2 LTS was rejected as a destination because it reached end of life in April 2026; the plan passes through it as a transit stop only. Django 6.1 was rejected because it is not an LTS. Python 3.14 was rejected because it is outside Django 5.2's tested matrix. He also decided to drop, not upgrade, a list of packages that turned out to be unused, permanently disabled or obsolete: hypothesis, fake-factory, django-qmethod, docutils and sqlparse are imported nowhere; mixpanel and mixpanel-py-async are dead because utils.send_event and utils.identify_user are stubs that return immediately; django-sendgrid-v5 is referenced nowhere and production uses Django's SMTP backend; django-debug-toolbar is permanently off behind a callback that reads 'False and (...)'; django-cloudflare-push does HTTP/2 server push, which browsers and Cloudflare both abandoned; django-recaptcha is behind ENABLE_CAPTCHA=False; django-extensions and werkzeug exist only for shell_plus and runserver_plus.

The production PostgreSQL was upgraded from 9.6 to 18 in Aug 2026, specifically to unblock the Django upgrade. Django enforces a minimum server version and refuses to connect below it, and PG 9.6 caps Django at 3.2, so this was a hard prerequisite rather than hygiene, although 9.6 had also been out of support since Nov 2021. Django 2.0 runs fine against PG 18: migrate was verified against the live database on the unmodified 2.0 image. That matters because Django 2.0's Postgres introspection reads pg_attrdef.adsrc, a column PostgreSQL 12 removed, and the Dokku predeploy hook runs migrate. Note for the last rung of the upgrade: PostgreSQL 18 is newer than Django 5.2, which shipped before it, so if anything is wrong at the database layer there, the answer is likely Django 6.0 rather than a workaround.

Stavros first said to delete Django's CSRF protection during the modernisation, on the grounds that the SameSite cookie attribute is enough, and then agreed to keep it. Reason: the site is behind Cloudflare and Dokku's nginx, which terminates TLS and proxies plain HTTP to the container, so request.is_secure() returns False for every request. Django 4.0 began comparing the Origin header against the scheme that is_secure() reports, which would have rejected every POST on the live site. Setting SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER and CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS is two lines and fixes it; deleting the middleware would have been more work, since it also means removing csrf_token from the templates, and SameSite=Lax does not cover a same-site subdomain or a state change reachable by GET. SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER is worth having on its own merits: without it, everything in Django that asks whether the request is secure gets the wrong answer.

Until Aug 2026 the CI tests job ran on SQLite while production ran PostgreSQL: with no DATABASE_URL and no IN_DOCKER set, pastery/settings.py falls through to the sqlite3 branch. So the 41-test suite said nothing about database behaviour, which was the wrong safety net to have while both the database major version and the ORM major version were about to move. The fix is to give the tests job a Postgres service and point Django at it by writing pastery/local_settings.py from the workflow, because settings.py already imports that file at the end inside a try/except. Do not use DATABASE_URL for this: that branch also switches sessions to Redis and parses EMAIL_URL with a regex that raises when unset.

Resolved by rep-mcpwp (Aug 2026): coverage raised to >=7,<8 and re-locked, replacing 4.4.2 (2017) with 7.10.7 on Python <3.10 (the 3.9 rung) and 7.15.4 on >=3.10. Both misreporting bugs this entry documented are gone, verified empirically with the test suite. The phantom statements attributed to main/models.py past its real end are gone: under 4.4.2 the missing range ran 749-2046 while the file is 729 lines; under 7.10.7 the missing lines top out at 653 and the statement count dropped 342 -> 271. And the .coveragerc omit pattern 'admin.py' now matches 'main/admin.py' by basename, so main/admin.py no longer appears in the report at all. The same 92 tests report 93% total (was 44% under 4.4.2). The coverage number can now be trusted.

The flaky 'poetry install --no-root' in the tests job is fixed, and the cause recorded in cauqbb was wrong. That entry blamed the mid-install setuptools swap. It was not the swap. Four runs of the same commit in Aug 2026 showed the real pattern: when ambient setuptools was 79.0.1 as curtsies 0.4.1 was built, the build succeeded; when it was the locked 67.6.0, whether because the swap landed mid-build or because it was pre-installed, the build failed with 'Backend setuptools.build_meta:__legacy__ is not available'. The trigger was the locked setuptools being visible in the ambient environment, and the swap was only one way of arriving there.

Do not try pinning the locked setuptools before the install. That was attempted and it made things worse: it removed the race but guaranteed the losing state, turning an intermittent failure into an every-run failure and taking master red.

The fix was to drop 'poetry config virtualenvs.create false' and prefix the later steps with 'poetry run'. With Poetry owning the runner's system Python, its ephemeral build environment could see the ambient site-packages and the locked setuptools collided with the one the build environment resolved for itself. In a real virtualenv the same downgrade happens harmlessly inside the isolated environment and the runner's own setuptools is left alone. curtsies and uwsgi, the only two packages in this lock with no wheels at all, now both build every run.

The language dropdown had "Markdown" twice (STA-114, Aug 2026). Offered the one-line fix of just dropping the duplicate, Stavros chose instead to keep both: "Markdown" still renders to prose, and a new "Markdown (source)" choice syntax-highlights the source. So the duplicate was a bug but the second entry is now deliberate.

Two alternatives were rejected on the way. Reusing "md" as the value for the source variant, which Pygments would accept directly and so would need no lexer override, was rejected because get_aliases() folds every Markdown alias into "markdown" and because language=md posted through the HTTP API currently means "render as prose"; repurposing it would silently flip behaviour for existing API clients. A per-paste "render this" boolean was rejected as more surface than a second language value for the same result: it needs a migration plus a new form field and a new API field.

The chosen value "markdown-source" is deliberately not a Pygments alias, so that ALIAS_DICT passes it through untouched and the `language == "markdown"` equality tests in paste.html, embed.html and views.py fall on the correct side with no template edits. It is public API: it appears in the HTTP API and in get_language_display(), so renaming it later breaks clients.

Upgrade gotcha for whoever does the pending Pygments bump: Pygments reorders lexer aliases between releases. The Markdown lexer reported ("md", "markdown") in 2.8.1 and reports ("markdown", "md") in 2.10 and 2.20. That reordering is what caused this bug in the first place, and this codebase assumed alias order in two places. Both were made order-independent, but check any new code that indexes aliases[0].

Do not propose a firewall allow-list of Cloudflare's ranges as the fix for the origin trusting client-supplied IP headers (STA-118, Aug 2026). It was the obvious lever and Stavros rejected it: the Hetzner host runs other things besides pastery, and a host-level rule restricting ports 80 and 443 to Cloudflare would affect all of them. The fix therefore lives in the application, in pastery/ratelimit.py, which trusts CF-Connecting-IP only when the peer is inside Cloudflare's published ranges.

Two consequences worth knowing. Direct-to-origin traffic still reaches the app, so Cloudflare's WAF and the Eastern Europe js_challenge rule in misc/terraform can still be bypassed by anyone who knows the origin IP; only the rate limit bucket is now safe. And the Cloudflare range list is committed in the repo, so it is a maintenance point: if Cloudflare adds a range and the list is not refreshed, visitors arriving through that new range all get bucketed by the edge IP they share and will be rate limited as one visitor. It fails towards over-limiting, not towards a hole.

Fetching Cloudflare's IP ranges at application startup, with the committed list as a fallback, was proposed by Stavros and rejected (STA-118, Aug 2026). Three reasons, the first decisive.

It would make the allow-list that decides whose CF-Connecting-IP we trust a value supplied over the network at runtime rather than a reviewed change in git; if anything ever injected a range, an attacker's own address would become 'Cloudflare' and the fix would silently evaporate.

The fallback is what makes the failure quiet, and this fetch is empirically unreliable: Cloudflare answers urllib's default User-Agent with a 403, found only by running the check for real. With fetch-and-fall-back, that 403 would have meant the app used the day-one list for ever with nobody knowing.

And it is not once per deploy. uwsgi.ini runs 3 processes with max-requests=5000, so workers respawn constantly and each respawn would fetch; the Dokku predeploy migrate imports the same module, so a hanging fetch could also stall a deploy that CHECKS is waiting on. Today neither the request path nor the boot path touches the network.

Doing it properly needs the refresh off the worker boot path and into a periodic job with alerting when it fails, which is more machinery than the weekly CI check it would replace. If it is ever revisited, those are the conditions.

Django 2.2 rung (S1-gfyky, Aug 2026): the adjacent pins the ticket expected to jump on their own (django-bootstrap3 12.1.0, django-redis 4.11.0, whitenoise 5.0, djangoql 0.14.0, pytz 2020.1, coverage 4.4.2) did NOT move. Plain 'uv lock' on uv 0.11.6 is preference-preserving: it keeps every locked version that still satisfies the constraints and only touched django 2.0.13 -> 2.2.28 plus its new dependency sqlparse. The pins only move under 'uv lock --upgrade', i.e. a fresh resolution, which would also drag in whitenoise 6.x, django-redis 5.2.0, bootstrap3 21.2, djangoql 0.19.1, pytz 2026.x and coverage 7.15.4; that was rejected as opportunistic modernisation. The 3.2 rung must decide the rest deliberately. Coverage was later moved separately by rep-mcpwp (constraint >=7,<8; 7.10.7 on Python <3.10, 7.15.4 on >=3.10), which resolved reanmn; the other pins still await an explicit decision.
